title: Migration ledger
description: One database's migration ledger as a document (not a model kind): the rows of its contract, applied_fact and applied_object tables, in the schema migrations.ledgerSchema names. Property names are the column names and each row's x-order is the column order, so a writer in any language maps them one to one. Contract version 1, a draft until it is frozen; see docs/ledger.md.

facts.description: The applied_fact rows: one per migration fact whose end state the database reached. Rows are never updated or deleted.

objects.description: The applied_object rows: one per object whose identity the writer owns, keyed by element_id. Readers ignore unknown kinds and read a missing row as unknown.

id.description: Always 1: the table holds one row.

version.description: The contract version the tables follow. A writer that finds a newer version stops.

fact_id.description: The migration fact's id (its model id).

content_hash.description: The fact content hash: SHA-256 over the fact's canonical document without its annotations, after, held and released, in 64 lowercase hex digits.

applied_at.description: The database's transaction time when the row was written.

applied_by.description: Free text naming the writer, or null.

objectRow.description: One applied object whose identity the writer owns.

kind.description: The model kind, such as sql-object; an open vocabulary.

content_hash.description: The hash of the version of the object that was applied.

revert_text.description: SQL that reverts the object and succeeds when it is already gone, or null. Contract version 1 writers write none.

applied_at.description: The database's transaction time when the row was written or last updated.
